description: (0.5.0, Draft, 2026-11-06) MCP revisions without an initialize handshake, and results that are not yet complete (RFC-ACDP-0019 §3.1–§3.2).

input.note: Run the proxy in front of a stub MCP server that speaks revision 2026-07-28 (no initialize; every request carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion in _meta) and returns the mcp-001 CallToolResult for tools/call regional_fraud_rate, with io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo {"name":"fraud-stats","version":"1.4.2"} in result _meta unless a scenario says otherwise, against a test registry. Scenario F uses a stub that speaks 2025-11-25; scenario H a stub serving both eras.

scenarios.name: A — revision and server identity from _meta

expected.behavior: With no initialize exchanged, the proxy publishes one body whose record has mcp_protocol_version "2026-07-28", server.name "fraud-stats" and server.version "1.4.2", and returns the link per §6.

scenarios.name: B — missing server identity is not a failure

expected.behavior: The result _meta carries no serverInfo and no server/discover response is available. The proxy publishes with server.name "unknown" and no server.version, and returns a link, not a failure value.
The result _meta carries no serverInfo, but a server/discover response from the same endpoint, within its ttlMs, names the server "fraud-stats". The record's server.name is "fraud-stats".

scenarios.name: D — input_required: the completing request is the call

expected.behavior: Request id 1 with arguments {"region":"EU"} returns resultType "input_required". The proxy relays it byte-for-byte unchanged, publishes no body and adds no io.agentcontextdistributionprotocol/provenance. The client sends request id 2 with arguments {"region":"EU-West"}, inputResponses and requestState, and gets resultType "complete". The proxy publishes exactly one body: arguments_hash recomputes over {"region":"EU-West"} and request_id_hash over 2 with the returned salt; neither matches the id-1 values; inputResponses and requestState are not hashed.

scenarios.name: E — task handle and completed task

expected.behavior: tools/call returns resultType "task". The proxy relays it unchanged and publishes no body. A covering proxy: the first tasks/get with status completed yields exactly one body (tool, arguments_hash and request_id_hash from the creating tools/call) and io.agentcontextdistributionprotocol/provenance in the inner result's _meta; a second tasks/get for the same task returns the identical io.agentcontextdistributionprotocol/provenance value and publishes nothing. Tasks ending failed or cancelled get no body. A task-status notification carrying a completed result is relayed without the result.

scenarios.name: E2 — task under fail-closed and lost state

expected.behavior: With fail-closed and the registry unreachable, the completed tasks/get keeps status completed and its inner result is the §7 failure result (isError true, one text item, io.agentcontextdistributionprotocol/provenance {"failed": true}). With the proxy restarted between task creation and completion, the completed task is a publish failure under the tool's policy.

scenarios.name: F — legacy revision: result before initialize

expected.behavior: Against a 2025-11-25 server, a tools/call result the proxy sees before the upstream initialize result is a publish failure (§7): fail-open returns the result with io.agentcontextdistributionprotocol/provenance {"failed": true}; fail-closed returns the §7 isError result instead.
A result with an unrecognized resultType is relayed unchanged and produces no body and no io.agentcontextdistributionprotocol/provenance.

On a server serving both eras, a legacy session's call records the initialize-negotiated protocolVersion and serverInfo, and a concurrent call whose _meta carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion "2026-07-28" records "2026-07-28" with no publish failure, although no initialize preceded it on its connection.
